audit_status.source_base: Greek 2 Corinthians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for letter of recommendation, tablets of hearts, new covenant, letter/Spirit, glory, veil, freedom, unveiled transformation. Anti-Jewish misuse warning included.

verses.restored: Are we beginning again to recommend ourselves? Or do we need, as some do, recommendation letters to you or from you?

familiar.text: Do we begin again to commend ourselves? or need we, as some others, epistles of commendation to you, or letters of commendation from you?

modern.text: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, like some people, letters of recommendation to you or from you?

original.text: Ἀρχόμεθα πάλιν ἑαυτοὺς ⸀συνιστάνειν; ⸀ἢ μὴ χρῄζομεν ὥς τινες συστατικῶν ἐπιστολῶν πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἢ ἐξ ⸀ὑμῶν;

verses.restored: You yourselves are our letter, having been written in our hearts, known and read by all humans,

familiar.text: Ye are our epistle written in our hearts, known and read of all men:

modern.text: You yourselves are our letter, inscribed on our hearts, known and read by everyone.

original.text: ἡ ἐπιστολὴ ἡμῶν ὑμεῖς ἐστε, ἐγγεγραμμένη ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ἡμῶν, γινωσκομένη καὶ ἀναγινωσκομένη ὑπὸ πάντων ἀνθρώπων·

verses.restored: being made manifest that you are a letter of Messiah, served by us, written not with ink but with Spirit of the living Divine, not on stone tablets but on tablets of human hearts.

familiar.text: Forasmuch as ye are manifestly declared to be the epistle of Christ ministered by us, written not with ink, but with the Spirit of the living God; not in tables of stone, but in fleshy tables of the heart.

modern.text: It is clear that you are a letter from Christ, the result of our ministry, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts.

original.text: φανερούμενοι ὅτι ἐστὲ ἐπιστολὴ Χριστοῦ διακονηθεῖσα ὑφʼ ἡμῶν, ἐγγεγραμμένη οὐ μέλανι ἀλλὰ πνεύματι θεοῦ ζῶντος, οὐκ ἐν πλαξὶν λιθίναις ἀλλʼ ἐν πλαξὶν καρδίαις σαρκίναις.

verses.restored: Such confidence we have through Messiah toward the Divine.

familiar.text: And such trust have we through Christ to God-ward:

modern.text: Such confidence before God is ours through Christ.

original.text: Πεποίθησιν δὲ τοιαύτην ἔχομεν διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ πρὸς τὸν θεόν.

verses.restored: Not that we are sufficient from ourselves to calculate anything as from ourselves, but our sufficiency is from the Divine,

familiar.text: Not that we are sufficient of ourselves to think any thing as of ourselves; but our sufficiency is of God;

modern.text: Not that we are competent in ourselves to claim that anything comes from us, but our competence comes from God.

original.text: οὐχ ὅτι ⸂ἀφʼ ἑαυτῶν ἱκανοί ἐσμεν⸃ λογίσασθαί τι ὡς ἐξ ⸀αὑτῶν, ἀλλʼ ἡ ἱκανότης ἡμῶν ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ,

verses.restored: who also made us sufficient as servants of a new covenant, not of letter but of Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit makes alive.

familiar.text: Who also hath made us able ministers of the new testament; not of the letter, but of the spirit: for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.

modern.text: And He has qualified us as ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life. The Glory of the New Covenant (Exodus 34:10–35)

original.text: ὃς καὶ ἱκάνωσεν ἡμᾶς διακόνους καινῆς διαθήκης, οὐ γράμματος ἀλλὰ πνεύματος, τὸ γὰρ γράμμα ἀποκτέννει, τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ζῳοποιεῖ.

verses.restored: But if the service of death, engraved in letters on stones, came in glory, so that the children of Israel were not able to gaze into the face of Moses because of the glory of his face, being made inactive,

familiar.text: But if the ministration of death, written and engraven in stones, was glorious, so that the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses for the glory of his countenance; which glory was to be done away:

modern.text: Now if the ministry of death, which was engraved in letters on stone, came with such glory that the Israelites could not gaze at the face of Moses because of its fleeting glory,

original.text: Εἰ δὲ ἡ διακονία τοῦ θανάτου ἐν ⸀γράμμασιν ⸀ἐντετυπωμένη λίθοις ἐγενήθη ἐν δόξῃ, ὥστε μὴ δύνασθαι ἀτενίσαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ εἰς τὸ πρόσωπον Μωϋσέως διὰ τὴν δόξαν τοῦ προσώπου αὐτοῦ τὴν καταργουμένην,

verses.restored: how will not the service of the Spirit be in more glory?

familiar.text: How shall not the ministration of the spirit be rather glorious?

modern.text: will not the ministry of the Spirit be even more glorious?

original.text: πῶς οὐχὶ μᾶλλον ἡ διακονία τοῦ πνεύματος ἔσται ἐν δόξῃ;

verses.restored: For if the service of condemnation has glory, much more does the service of righteousness/justice abound in glory.

familiar.text: For if the ministration of condemnation be glory, much more doth the ministration of righteousness exceed in glory.

modern.text: For if the ministry of condemnation was glorious, how much more glorious is the ministry of righteousness!

original.text: εἰ γὰρ ⸂τῇ διακονίᾳ⸃ τῆς κατακρίσεως δόξα, πολλῷ μᾶλλον περισσεύει ἡ διακονία τῆς ⸀δικαιοσύνης δόξῃ.

verses.restored: For indeed what had been glorified has not been glorified in this respect, because of the surpassing glory.

familiar.text: For even that which was made glorious had no glory in this respect, by reason of the glory that excelleth.

modern.text: Indeed, what was once glorious has no glory now in comparison to the glory that surpasses it.

original.text: καὶ γὰρ οὐ δεδόξασται τὸ δεδοξασμένον ἐν τούτῳ τῷ μέρει ⸀εἵνεκεν τῆς ὑπερβαλλούσης δόξης·

verses.restored: For if what was being made inactive came through glory, much more what remains is in glory.

familiar.text: For if that which is done away was glorious, much more that which remaineth is glorious.

modern.text: For if what was fading away came with glory, how much greater is the glory of that which endures!

original.text: εἰ γὰρ τὸ καταργούμενον διὰ δόξης, πολλῷ μᾶλλον τὸ μένον ἐν δόξῃ.

verses.restored: Therefore, having such hope, we use much boldness,

familiar.text: Seeing then that we have such hope, we use great plainness of speech:

modern.text: Therefore, since we have such a hope, we are very bold.

original.text: Ἔχοντες οὖν τοιαύτην ἐλπίδα πολλῇ παρρησίᾳ χρώμεθα,

verses.restored: and not as Moses would put a veil over his face so that the children of Israel might not gaze at the completion of what was being made inactive.

familiar.text: And not as Moses, which put a vail over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end of that which is abolished:

modern.text: We are not like Moses, who would put a veil over his face to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away.

original.text: καὶ οὐ καθάπερ Μωϋσῆς ἐτίθει κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τὸ πρόσωπον ⸀αὐτοῦ, πρὸς τὸ μὴ ἀτενίσαι τοὺς υἱοὺς Ἰσραὴλ εἰς τὸ τέλος τοῦ καταργουμένου.

verses.restored: But their thoughts were hardened; for until this very day, at the reading of the old covenant, the same veil remains, not being unveiled, because in Messiah it is made inactive.

familiar.text: But their minds were blinded: for until this day remaineth the same vail untaken away in the reading of the old testament; which vail is done away in Christ.

modern.text: But their minds were closed. For to this day the same veil remains at the reading of the old covenant. It has not been lifted, because only in Christ can it be removed.

original.text: ἀλλὰ ἐπωρώθη τὰ νοήματα αὐτῶν. ἄχρι γὰρ τῆς σήμερον ⸀ἡμέρας τὸ αὐτὸ κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τῇ ἀναγνώσει τῆς παλαιᾶς διαθήκης μένει μὴ ἀνακαλυπτόμενον, ⸀ὅτι ἐν Χριστῷ καταργεῖται,

verses.restored: But until today, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies upon their heart.

familiar.text: But even unto this day, when Moses is read, the vail is upon their heart.

modern.text: And even to this day when Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts.

original.text: ἀλλʼ ἕως σήμερον ἡνίκα ⸂ἂν ἀναγινώσκηται⸃ Μωϋσῆς κάλυμμα ἐπὶ τὴν καρδίαν αὐτῶν κεῖται·

verses.restored: But whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

familiar.text: Nevertheless when it shall turn to the Lord, the vail shall be taken away.

modern.text: But whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

original.text: ἡνίκα ⸂δὲ ἐὰν⸃ ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς κύριον, περιαιρεῖται τὸ κάλυμμα.

verses.restored: Now the Lord is the Spirit; and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.

familiar.text: Now the Lord is that Spirit: and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.

modern.text: Now the Lord is the Spirit, and where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom.

original.text: ὁ δὲ κύριος τὸ πνεῦμά ἐστιν· οὗ δὲ τὸ πνεῦμα ⸀κυρίου, ἐλευθερία.

verses.restored: But we all, with unveiled face, beholding/reflecting the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are being transformed into the same image from glory into glory, just as from Lord, Spirit.

familiar.text: But we all, with open face beholding as in a glass the glory of the Lord, are changed into the same image from glory to glory, even as by the Spirit of the LORD.

modern.text: And we, who with unveiled faces all reflect the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

original.text: ἡμεῖς δὲ πάντες ἀνακεκαλυμμένῳ προσώπῳ τὴν δόξαν κυρίου κατοπτριζόμενοι τὴν αὐτὴν εἰκόνα μεταμορφούμεθα ἀπὸ δόξης εἰς δόξαν, καθάπερ ἀπὸ κυρίου πνεύματος.

safety_note: 2 Corinthians 3 must not be used as anti-Jewish contempt. Paul is using Moses/veil/new covenant imagery to describe transformation in Messiah and Spirit, while still drawing from Israel's Scriptures. Handle the veil language as rhetorical and pastoral, not as a license to demean Jewish readers or Torah.
